it as follows. In the urban dialect survey,
informants were asked to take part in a 'self-evaluation' test
in order to investigate what they believed themselves to be
opposed to what they actually did say. In this test,
they read aloud to the informants with two or more different
variants. For example:
how 1. [hjuːn] 2. [hjuːn]
The first variant has a y-glide [j], the second 'h-less'.
Both pronunciations are current in Norwich, the home
of the RP pronunciation, having more prestige than the
informants were then asked to say, by marking a
chart, which of the pronunciations they normally
uses. By comparing the results of this test with the
tape-recorded during the interviews, it became possible
to discover discrepancies between what informants say
they say and what they actually said. The results for the
social classes, which we will see were very interesting, and not
always straightforward, are divided into two groups.
The informants tended to be very consistent in their tape-recorded
speech, but they were not when they were self-assessing. They
varied their self-assessment, some choosing the y-glide ones, and those with less formal
class background tended to be more open. They were honest about it.

Purpose of Game: 
Best played for fun - a good strenuous game. 

Description of Game: Each team plants a flag in a vis-  ible but inconspicuous spot in their territory. They  must stay at least 5 meters away from their flag unless in  pursuit of an opponent. 

Each team is to try to find and capture their opponent's
flag - while defending, by capturing opponents who
are trying to take their flag. The winner is the team
which captures the flag and returns it to its home base.
If time expires before this is done, the winner is the
team that captured more of their opponents.


Capturing - players have a strip of wool on their right
arm. If this is captured by an opponent, they can return
to home base and, after a 2 - minute penalty, get a new
ribbon.


Variation: Players can be captured with a 2-hand touch. The prisoner must go to a jail defined by her captors. She can then be freed by a member of her own team who touches her. Several captured players can be freed at once if they are holding hand.

Creamy Garlic & Roasted Red Pepper Pasta
PREP TIME: 15 MINUTES | 4 SERVINGS
12 oz pasta (penne or fusilli)
2 tbsp olive oil
3 cloves garlic, minced
1 cup roasted red peppers, chopped
1/2 cup heavy cream
1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
Salt
Pepper
Red pepper flakes
Fresh parsley
to taste
1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the pasta and cook according to package instructions until al dente. Drain, reserving 1/4 cup of the pasta water.
2. Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
3. Stir in the roasted red peppers and cook for 2 minutes. Pour in the heavy cream and bring to a simmer.
4. Add the Parmesan cheese and stir until melted and the sauce has thickened slightly.
5. Add the cooked pasta to the skillet and toss to coat with the sauce. If the sauce is too thick, add the reserved pasta water, a tablespoon at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
6. Season with salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes to taste. Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
Enjoy this creamy and flavorful pasta dish as a quick weeknight dinner or a simple yet elegant meal for guests.
For an extra kick, add some crushed red pepper flakes or serve with a side of crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
Enjoy!

100g (3½oz) plain flour
1 tsp baking powder
1 tsp ground cinnamon
1 tsp ground ginger
½ tsp ground cloves
¼ tsp freshly grated nutmeg
100g (3½oz) unsalted butter, softened
100g (3½oz) light muscovado sugar
100g (3½oz) black treacle
1 large egg, beaten
1 tbsp milk
100g (3½oz) icing sugar, sifted
1 tbsp lemon juice
a little green food colouring
red and green candied cherries, to decorate
Preheat the oven to 180°C/350°F/gas 4.
Grease and base-line a 1lb loaf tin.
Sift the flour, baking powder and spices into a bowl.
Cream the butter and sugar together until light and fluffy.
Gradually beat in the treacle, egg and milk.
Fold in the flour mixture.
Spoon into the tin and level the top.
Bake for 40-45 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean.
Leave to cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.

VizWiz_val_00000300.jpg: # BEAT THE BURGLAR BASIC TIPS: When you go out, always lock the door and close the windows even if you are just going out for a short time. Window locks, especially on older windows, will help stop people getting in (and remember, a burglar is less likely to break in if they have to smash a window). If you have deadlocks, use them. They make it harder for a thief to get out again. But don't leave the key near the door, or in an obvious place. - Don't leave spare keys outside, or in a garage or shed, and put car keys or garage keys out of sight in the house. - Use timers for lights and radios if you need to be away from home overnight. They will create the impression that someone is in. Visible burglar alarms, good lighting, and carefully directed and limited security lighting can act as deterrents. But make sure that lights don't disturb your neighbours, and that alarms turn off after 20 minutes. Fences at the back of the house may make this area more secure, but walls and solid fencing may let a thief break in without being seen. A good compromise is chain-link fencing, or trellises with prickly shrubs. • Fitting a 'spy hole' allows you to see who is at the door. Having a door chain means you can open the door a little way to talk. safely. Make sure that any improvements you make don't stop you from getting out of your house as quickly as possible if there is a fire.

Blio, libros para todos.
Una compañía cuyo propósito es proveer acceso a la letra impresa a las personas ciegas.
En la década de los 2000's KNFB Reading Technology introdujo el KNFB Reader. Un equipo, el cual
luego se combinará con un teléfono celular, que te permite tomar una foto a un documento impreso, y este te
lee en voz alta o te lo traduce a Braille electrónico.


Basandose en el exito del KNFB Reader, KNFB Reading Technology decidio intentar algo distinto. El
proveer acceso a los libros electronicos. De eso salio Blio. Como iBooks, funciona hambo de tienda y como lector.
Blio provee acceso a libros electronicos en casi todas las plataformas tecnologicas.


Al principio Blio fue criticado por que no era accesible para las personas ciegas. Pero esto fue rectificado
Blio tiene aplicaciones para el iPhone, el iPad y
apidamente. Ademas de proveer acceso via lectores de pantallas.
os telefonos Android. Asi que los estudiantes pueden cargar los libros, no importa el equipo que utilizen.


Blio en la computadora funciona igual a iBooks en el iPad. Blio te permite engresar parrafos o frases, te
permite tomar notas en el libro, buscar definiciones y verificar el como se escribe una palabra. En la version
mobil, Blio es un poco mas limitado, por ejemplo, no puedes tomar notas, pero el hecho que puedas tener el libro
no importa el equipo que estes utilizando, lo hace mas atractivo para escuelas que no tengan el dinero para
comprar iPads o ya ayan comprado otros equipos y no quieran reinvertir en otros equipos. Al momento de esta
escritura, Blio esta disponible en las siguientes plataformas: Windows XP, Vista, 7 y 8, iPhone, iPod touch, y
Pad, y muchos telefonos y tabletas Android. Todavia no existe una version para la Mac.


No sin embargo, no es el unico que puede ser utilizado en multiples plataformas. Existen otros programas

For instance, OCR programs require users to carefully center the text they want to read in the cam- era's view, and then return all of the text. In contrast, VizWiz users can simply ask what they really want to know, for in- stance, "How much is the cheeseburger?" Because blind peo- ple cannot see the picture they are taking, pictures are often not framed well or have other problems. Real people can give guidance as to how to take a better picture. With real people answering questions, we can first target tools to what blind people want and then try to automate, rather than create tools according to what can currently be done automatically and hope they are good enough. # Contributions Our contributions are the following - We motivate and present VizWiz, a talking mobile applica- tion that lets blind people take a picture, ask a question, and receive answers from remote workers in nearly real-time. - We introduce *quikTurkit*, an approach and accompanying implementation that shows how workers can be intelligently recruited in advance to reduce latency. - We show that VizWiz can work in real-world situations and we demonstrate some of the primary problems that blind people have taking photographs in a field deployment - We introduce VizWiz::LocateIt, a VizWiz extension that combines remote human-powered vision with automatic computer vision, illustrating how VizWiz facilitates par- ticipatory design with prototype tools which cannot yet be made fully automatic. **MOTIVATING SURVEY** We first recruited 11 participants (5 female) to get an idea of how blind people might want to use a system like VizWiz. We presented the idea of VizWiz, and asked participants how they could imagine using it. Participants wanted to read text in a variety of situations - road signs, cafe menu boards, tags on clothes, and cooking instructions on a packaged meal. Several participants wanted information about their physical appearance. For instance, how does this outfit look or is this shirt stained or discoloured? Many participants just wanted feedback on how good the picture was that they took or gen- eral information on the photos they have taken. Google's An- droid platform and the Apple iPhone 3GS now include free screen readers [36, 6]. The iPhone has proven particularly popular among blind users, which motivated us to concen- trate on it for VizWiz. Apple's stringent controls on the ap- plications available on its online store and tighter integration of its screen reader (VoiceOver) with the operating system has resulted in a large number of accessible applications. Touchscreen devices like the iPhone were once assumed to be inaccessible to blind users, but well-designed, multitouch interfaces leverage the spatial layout of the screen and can even be preferred by blind people [12]. Applications for general-purpose smartphones are beginning to replace special-purpose devices, but blind people still carry devices such as GPS powered navigation aids, barcode read- ers, light detectors, color identifiers, and compasses [13]. Some accessible applications that use the camera on existing phones include currency reading applications and color iden- tifiers [20, 37]. Because VizWiz connects users to real peo- ple, it can potentially answer all of the questions answerable by many costly special-purpose applications and devices. *Talking OCR Devices*: Of particular interest to blind people is the ability to read text, which pervasively labels objects and provides information. Both the KNFBReader [16] and the Intel Reader [11] are talking mobile OCR tools. VizWiz has an advantage over tools such as these because humans can still read more text written in more variations than can automatic approaches. When OCR works, however, it is faster and can be used to transcribe large text passages. Hu- man workers are slower but this may be partially offset by their ability to take instructions that require intelligence. For example, an OCR program can read an entire menu, but can- not be asked, "What is the price of the cheapest salad?" *Other Automatic Computer Vision for Mobile Devices: Sev- eral research projects and products expose automatic com- puter vision on mobile devices. 美食的黄金守则 在追求美食的道路上,有几条黄金守则 能让我们不仅吃得开心,更能吃出健康。 这些守则不仅适用于家庭烹饪,也适用于 在外就餐的选择。遵循这些原则,让饮食 成为一种享受。 一、食材新鲜是基础 食材的质量直接决定了菜肴的口感和营养 价值。新鲜的蔬菜、水果、肉类和海鲜,不仅 口感鲜美,且含有更丰富的营养成分。尽量 选择当季食材,不仅价格更亲民,且品质 往往也是最好的。避免购买过度加工的食 品,减少添加剂的摄入。 二、均衡饮食是核心 没有一种食物能提供人体所需的所有营养 素。因此,食物的多样性至关重要。每餐 都应包含碳水化合物、蛋白质、脂肪、维生 素和矿物质。通过搭配不同颜色的蔬果和 谷物,可以确保摄入全面的营养。 三、烹饪方式要讲究 健康的烹饪方式可以最大程度地保留食材 的营养,减少有害物质的产生。推荐使用 蒸、煮、炖、拌等方式,减少油炸、烧烤和 过度煎炒。这不仅能减少油脂的摄入,还 能避免因高温烹饪产生的致癌物质。 四、适量摄入是关键 即使是再健康的食物,过量食用也会对身 体造成负担。学会控制食量,吃到七八分饱 即可。这有助于减轻肠胃负担,防止肥胖 及相关慢性疾病的发生。 五、享受过程更重要 美食不仅是为了填饱肚子,更是一种生活 的艺术。在用餐时,放下手机和工作的烦 恼,专注于食物的味道、香气和质感。细嚼 慢咽,不仅有助于消化,更能让你从每一 口食物中感受到幸福。 六、水分补充不可少 水是生命之源,参与体内的新陈代谢。保 持充足的水分摄入,有助于皮肤健康和身 体功能的正常运转。尽量选择白开水或淡 茶,少喝含糖饮料,这能有效减少热量摄 入。 遵循这些黄金守则,不仅能让你在享受美 食的同时,也能守护好自己的健康。让每 一次进餐,都成为对自己身体的呵护。 从今天开始,尝试做出一点改变吧。 [VISUAL_TEXT] [VISUAL_TEXT] [VISUAL_TEXT] 备注: 健康饮食 对于特定人群(如糖尿病患者、高血压患 者等),饮食应更加谨慎。建议咨询专业 医生或营养师,根据个人的身体状况,制定 个性化的饮食方案。不要盲目跟风所谓的 “超级食物”或极端饮食法。 结语: 美食是生活的调味剂,健康的身体则是生 活的基石。在美食与健康之间找到平衡, 这才是真正的生活智慧。愿你既能品尝世 间美味,又能拥有强健体魄,享受美好生 活。 保持良好的心态,也是健康生活的一部分。 让我们一起,为了健康和美味而努力。 享受每一餐,享受生活。 香港麥當勞食品之營養資料 Nutritional Information of Selected Menu Items in Hong Kong 食品名稱 (Food Item) 能量 (Energy) (kcal) 蛋白質 (Protein) (g) 總脂肪 (Total Fat) (g) 漢堡包 (Hamburger) 芝士漢堡包 (Cheeseburger) 雙層芝士漢堡包 (Double Cheeseburger)

Free
Wish you had someone handy to tell you what
something was or to clarify something any time of the
day or night? VizWiz is an amazing application that is
extremely effective. Simply take a picture of any object
and record your question. Then select whom you wish to send it to. Your
choices are Web Worker, IQ Engine, email or Twitter. Web worker is a
human volunteer who will review and answer your question. In testing we
took a photo of a bottle of foundation makeup. We then asked "Is there any
sunscreen in this foundation?" In less than 30 seconds we received an
accurate answer from a Web Worker "Yes, the foundation has 15 SPF
sunscreen. Another choice for response is IQ Engine, a character reader.
The response from the IQ Engine was to recite the product UPC code. While
the IQ Engine was not accurate, we do see where it could be handy for
getting serial numbers or other numerical data. Email allows you to send
your question to someone you know from your contacts and Twitter will
tweet your question to your followers. We were impressed by VizWiz, and
did we mention it is free?

one important feature of social context which may well
have some bearing on the formality of the language used is the
nature of the person spoken to, and in particular the role
relationships and relative statuses of the participants in a dis-
course. For example, speech between individuals in a dis-
similar status in an organization, social class, age, or some
other factor) is likely to be less relaxed and more formal than
that between equals, and in certain languages definite rules may
dictate which linguistic forms may or may not be used. A
common example of this is the different forms of address that are
produced by different degrees of status difference or intimacy.
Different degrees of politeness and deference may be required,
and these are signalled linguistically. The connotations of Eng-
lish address forms such as sir, Mr Smith, Smith, Frederick, Fred,
while all different, each has different stylistic
implications, and the rules for their usage, as well as the fre-
quency of their usage, are quite complex. These rules often vary
from class to class, age-group to age-group, and place to place.
There are notable differences between the usage of British and
American speakers of English, for example: the term sir, for
instance, is used more freely as a term of address - to attract
attention in American English than in British English.

native peoples in California under the Spanish mission system
versus the inhuman treatment they received from Anglo-Americans
(Bright, 1984). In this instance, then, the nature of the sociocultural
contact between the native peoples and the newcomers was reflected in the
loss of Native American languages.

life's tide can take us by surprise, as we find ourselves unpre-

Stove Top

cups water, 1 tbsp butter or oil and
1/2 tsp salt to a boil.
2. Stir in 1 cup rice. Cover and
reduce heat to low and simmer for

absorbed.
3. Fluff with a fork & serve.
Microwave
1. Combine 2 cups water, 1 tbsp
butter or oil, 1/2 tsp salt and 1 cup
rice in a microwave safe bowl.
2. Cover and microwave on high for
15 minutes.
3. Let stand for 5 minutes.
4. Fluff with a fork & serve.

OFF-LEASH DOG AREA RULES


PARK HOURS ARE DAWN TO DUSK
1. OWNERS OF DOGS IN DESIGNATED OFF-LEASH AREAS MUST BE
PRESENT AT ALL TIMES WITHIN VOCAL CONTROL DISTANCE OF THEIR
DOGS, AND ENSURE THAT THEIR DOGS DO NOT CAUSE PUBLIC
NUISANCE, SAFETY HAZARD OR HARASS PEOPLE, OTHER DOGS OR
WILDLIFE.
3. UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES MAY AN OWNER BRING A SICK DOG INTO
THE PARK (SEVERE RUNNY NOSE/EYES, DIARRHEA, VOMITING,
COUGH, ETC.).
4. YOU ARE REQUIRED BY LAW (S.C.C. 22.16.030) TO SCOOP YOUR
PET'S WASTE.
5. PARK VISITORS USE THE PARK AT THEIR OWN RISK. OWNERS ARE
RESPONSIBLE AND LIABLE FOR THEIR CHILDREN, DOGS AND THEIR
ACTIONS. LEAVING DOGS OR CHILDREN UNATTENDED IS
PROHIBITED.
6. LIMIT OF THREE (3) DOGS PER ADULT.
7. DOGS SHALL BE ON LEASH IN ALL AREAS OF THE PARK OUTSIDE
THE DESIGNATED OFF-LEASH AREAS.
8. OWNERS SHALL CARRY A LEASH AND MONITOR THEIR DOGS AT ALL
TIMES.
9. DOGS IN HEAT SHALL BE LEFT AT HOME.
10. DOGS THAT EXHIBIT DANGEROUS OR AGGRESSIVE BEHAVIOR,
INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO BITING AND FIGHTING, SHALL BE
LEASHED IMMEDIATELY AND REMOVED FROM THE PARK; AND MAY
BE ASKED NOT TO RETURN TO THE OFF-LEASH DOG AREA.
11. DOGS WITH A HISTORY OF DANGEROUS BEHAVIOR ARE PROHIBITED.
12. PUPPIES LESS THAN SIX (6) MONTHS OF AGE ARE PROHIBITED.
PUPPIES OVER SIX (6) MONTHS OF AGE SHALL HAVE CURRENT
VACCINATIONS.
13. EXCESSIVE BARKING OR DIGGING SHALL BE CONTROLLED AS A
COURTESY TO OTHER PARK VISITORS. OWNERS SHALL FILL HOLES
PRIOR TO LEAVING PARK.
14. CALL 911 FOR ALL EMERGENCIES. CALL SNOHOMISH COUNTY
REGION 5 PARK RANGERS at 360-568-2482 TO REPORT ANY DOG
AGGRESSION OR ATTACKS. IF NO ANSWER LEAVE A MESSAGE AND A
RANGER WILL RETURN YOUR CALL.
15. UNTIL RUNNING WATER BECOMES AVAILABLE, OWNERS ARE
RESPONSIBLE FOR PROVIDING DRINKING WATER FOR THEIR CANINE
COMPANIONS. IN ORDER TO PREVENT THE SPREAD OF ILLNESS,
PLEASE DO NOT SHARE WATER BOWLS WITH OTHER PARK USERS.
16. REFER TO SNOHOMISH COUNTY CODE TITLE 9, ANIMALS AND TITLE
22, PARKS FOR ADDITIONAL REGULATIONS. VIOLATION OF PARK
RULES OR COUNTY CODES SHALL BE REPORTED TO THE PARKS

VizWiz_train_00012595.jpg: I remember laughing as my mom struggled to thread a needle. Glasses resting on her nose, she trimmed the end of the thread, sucked on it, failed to get it threaded, and re- trimmed it. Eventually she would ask one of us kids to thread it for her. Then, forty years later, when it was me with the problem, it wasn't so funny. I thought, "We've been to the moon; surely someone had fixed the needle." The only "easy to thread needle" had a slit at the top of the eye. It came unthreaded rig away and shredded my thread. Then I found out it had been invented in 1850. Why has someone come up with a better needle design in 150 years? After six months of grinding points on pieces of wire, I finally found a way to manufacture my One Second Needle threading needle. **A Tutorial on The Kitáb-i-Íqán**
**A Journey through the Book of Certitude**
The Kitáb-i-Íqán is one of the most important Writings of Bahá'u'lláh, the Bahá'í Faith. In the closing years of His stay in Baghdad (AD 1853-1863), Shoghi Effendi, the Guardian of the Bahá'í Faith, describes it as the "first repository of the Covenant of God" and the "precursor" to the Kitáb-i-Aqdas, the Most Holy Book.
This current book is a record of the journey that the author has taken through a background of the 12 chapters of the Kitáb-i-Íqán. It is a guide for the reader to help navigate through each paragraph and understand the content of each chapter. The book is written in a simple and accessible way, rather than a scholarly analysis, to provide the reader with a practical study of the Kitáb-i-Íqán.
The 290 paragraphs of the Kitáb-i-Íqán are addressed in the book. The author has taken each address in the text and provided an explanation. It is not an exhaustive study of all materials or all the opinions and commentary available on the Kitáb-i-Íqán; rather, it is a compilation of the notes and reflections that the author has obtained from other Bahá'í sources. It is called a tutorial because the author has tried to reflect the content for study to both Bahá'ís and non-Bahá'ís. The references are sourced either from Bahá'u'lláh or the Universal House of Justice, or related chapters on Bahá'í youth and has been developed with the intent to understand the intricate capacity to understand.

Since 1948 Marie Callender's has been making delicious pies with crisp, fresh apples and other fine ingredients. We know you'll enjoy this pie just as much as we enjoyed making it for you.
bake it your way
In 1948, when Marie Callender first baked pies for local restaurants, her goal was simple: to make the best ingredients and put such love and care into each and every pie that people would know she baked them herself. Marie Callender's name has become synonymous with quality and great home cooking, and we're proud to continue that tradition today. We've been warming hearts and homes with Marie's delicious pies for years, and we're pleased to share that warmth and comfort with you and your family.
As always, we love to hear from our customers. If you have any questions or comments, please write to us at the address listed on the side panel.
Baking Directions
Conventional Oven
 1. Preheat oven to 375°F.
 2. Remove pie from carton and place frozen pie on cookie sheet on
center oven rack.
 3. Bake on cookie sheet for 65 to 75 minutes. Pie is done when the edge
is golden brown and the center is bubbling.
 4. Remove pie from oven on cookie sheet using oven mitts.
 5. Let pie stand for 1 hour to cool. The crumb topping will bake to a
golden brown and the filling will be warm and delicious.
Remove pie from oven carefully. The pie is hot. Let stand at least 1 hour.
The pie will slice and serve best when cooled.
Marie's Baking Tips:
 • To prevent edge of pie crust from browning too much, cover edges with
aluminum foil and remove during last 15-20 minutes of baking.
 • Our pies are filled with luscious ripe fruit, which may bubble over
during baking. Be sure to cover your cookie sheet with foil.
KEEP FROZEN UNTIL READY TO BAKE.

languages of the now independent country, known as Neo-Melanesian,
Tok Pisin (from talk pidgin), it has become the lingua franca of about 1
million people who speak some 700 languages native to Papua New Guinea
as the first language of some 20,000 households (Mühlhäusler 1997: 76).
Tok Pisin has acquired such prestige that more parliamentary debates are
now conducted in it than in English, and most recently it has been used
in the country's university lecture halls.
At least three-fourths of the Tok Pisin vocabulary derives from English,
but 15 percent from the indigenous New Guinea languages, especially Tolai
and the remainder from various other languages, including German.
For example, in the singular, Tok Pisin personal pronouns are 'I, me', 'you'
'em' or 'he, him, she, her; it'. In the plural, they are 'mi-pela' 'we', 'yu-pela'
'you (plural)', 'ol' 'they'. In the first-person plural, the same whether they serve as
subject or object: 'yumi' 'we, us (including the hearer)' and the exclusive form
'mipela' 'we, us (excluding the hearer)', and in all three persons of the plural
the dual number (up to three) is usually indicated, as in 'yutripela' 'you two'
'yupela' 'you three', the form of for the third-person plural occurs in ad-
dition to the expected form. Possession is indicated by 'bilong', 'you two'
is usually marked by the particle 'i', and transitive verbs have the suffix
'-im', which also converts adjectives into causative verb forms. Accordingly,
'Em i bruk lek bilong mi' means 'One of my legs is broken', 'Em i krosim mi as 'He scolded me', and
'Em i mekim dispela samting' is 'He did this thing'.

Linguistically speaking the two are very similar, and they are
mutually comprehensible. The dichotomy, moreover,
has much more to the written standard languages than to
spoken language. Most people speak rural dialects or non-
standard urban dialects, although western dialects do tend to
resemble Nynorsk more closely, and some eastern dialects are
more similar to Bokmål. Perhaps sociolinguistically more inter-
esting than the differences *between* the two languages, however,
are the differences *within* them. In both Bokmål and Nynorsk
there are variants (alternative pronunciations and grammatical
constructions) which are known as *radical* and *conservative*. In
the case of Bokmål, right-wing newspapers tend to use conserva-
tive forms, and left-wing papers radical forms. It is also often
possible to make an intelligent guess about educated speakers'
background from the forms they use. This involvement of language
in politics, in a rather unusually overt form, means that few
Norwegians are very objective about the linguistic situation in
their country, and that the 'language question' is often very
heated indeed. The heat of the argument can be judged
from the fact that in 1955 a weather-forecaster on the Norwegian
radio became known as the 'abominable snowman' and was
nearly dismissed because he refused to say *snø* (a radical Bokmål
word) 'now' instead of *sne* (a conservative form).
The Norwegian situation is clearly unusual, and, many Nor-
wegians would say, a very awkward one, because it is expensive
to a country with such a small population to print schoolbooks
and official documents in both languages, and time-consuming
for pupils to have to teach both. In my own view it is in
many ways a very good situation, since it means that far more
Norwegians than would otherwise be the case are able to learn
to read, and, if they wish, write, speak and express themselves
in the standard language that closely resembles their own native
dialectal variation being quite considerable in Norway).

*The Lexical Nature of Concepts*


211


the ability to categorize: to judge whether or not a particular thing is an in-
stance of a particular category (*Rover* is a "dog"; *Garfield* is a "cat"). (4) The
ability to apply categories successfully is "indispensable in using previous ex-
perience to guide the interpretation of new experience: without categorization,
memory is virtually useless" (Jackendoff 1983:77). (5) We should remember,
however, that although categories are indispensible for living, not all catego-
rization is necessarily linguistic. Animals must do so all the time—this is "eat-
able," this is "harmful"—without using *linguistic* categories.


Finally, we should note that some semanticists and linguists use the term
“lexeme” or “lexical item”—rather than “word”—when they want to distin-
guish a word as an abstraction from any of its specific forms or parts of speech.
For example, there is some underlying notion of “runningness” in the terms
“run,” “ran,” “running,” “runs” and so on, that would be missed if we consid-
ered them to be different terms entirely. We will now look at how concepts be-
come incorporated into language by way of words, grammar, and discourse.


The Lexical Nature of Concepts
One of the primary ways meaning is demonstrated in language is through its
words. Words are basic to all communication, and seem to be the first things
children learn when acquiring their language. Indeed, as anyone who has
ever been to a foreign country can tell you, knowledge of a few words can
sometimes get you a long way, even if your command of the other aspects of
the language are limited.

language are limited.
Sense vs. Reference. In our discussions of the semiotic triangle we saw that
the term referent was used when speaking about concrete real things, such as
a tree. Reference, then, deals with the connection between a specific expression
and a specific case or individual instance. But we can also look at trees as an ab-
straction. In short, reference deals with things in the real world, but sense is related to other words.

At Disaster Bay February of 1911, the steamer SS
New Guinea became a total wreck after striking reefs in
dense fog. The bottom was torn clean out of the 300ft
vessel and she was wedged in the bay just 1/2 mile from
the lighthouse. She was a fully laden ship with cargo of
£79,000, but astonishingly the crew salvaged very little
except one full cask of wine, which they immediately
set to reaching the safety of the shore.
Disaster Bay has changed little since 1911, the rugged
cliff stands as a stark reminder of the perils of the
Southern Ocean and fine wine is still prized above
anything else.
Disaster Bay Original Hot Chilli Wine
Our authentic Hot Chilli Wine contains no grapes.
A true chilli wine blended from fresh chillies grown
organically on our chilli plantation.
This bold wine is best enjoyed chilled from a glass.
The rich fruit flavours will enliven your palate. The
smooth sweetness balances the heat of the chillies,
a warm inner glow. A perfect accompaniment to
fried oysters.
Once opened Hot Chilli Wine can happily remain in the
refrigerator for several months.

languages of the now independent country, known as Neo-Melanesian,
Tok Pisin (from talk pidgin), it has become the lingua franca of about 1
million people who speak some 700 languages native to Papua New Guinea
as the first language of some 20,000 households (Mühlhäusler 1997: 76).
Tok Pisin has acquired such prestige that more parliamentary debates are
now conducted in it than in English, and most recently it has been used
in the country's university lecture halls.
At least three-fourths of the Tok Pisin vocabulary derives from English,
but 15 percent from the indigenous New Guinea languages, especially Tolai
and the remainder from various other languages, including German.
For example, in the singular, Tok Pisin personal pronouns are 'I, me', 'you'
'em' or 'he, him, she, her; it'. In the plural, they are 'mi-pela' 'we', 'yu-pela'
'you (plural)', 'ol' 'they'. In the first-person plural, the same whether they serve as
subject or object: 'yumi' 'we, us (including the hearer)' and the exclusive form
'mipela' 'we, us (excluding the hearer)', and in all three persons of the plural
the dual number (up to three) is usually indicated, as in 'yutripela' 'you two'
'yupela' 'you three', the form of for the third-person plural occurs in ad-
dition to the expected form. Possession is indicated by 'bilong', 'you two'
is usually marked by the particle 'i', and transitive verbs have the suffix
'-im', which also converts adjectives into causative verb forms. Accordingly,
'Em i bruk lek bilong mi' means 'One of my legs is broken', 'Em i krosim mi as 'He scolded me', and
'Em i mekim dispela samting' is 'He did this thing'.

Life is all about changes. Nothing ever stays the same! Some changes are good, and some changes are bad. And sometimes, it just depends on who you are and how you look at it. Maybe you loved going to kindergarten, but your brother or sister hated it. You might have been excited when someone new married into your family, or you might not have been. Change comes in various forms, and people react to it in many different ways, but one aspect of change is constant—it is unavoidable! tives: means to lead change. edures for Sometimes, we don't have any control over the changes that come into our lives. When you're a kid, and your parents decide to move, you pretty much have to move, right? And even as an adult, the presidential candidate you support and vote for might not be the one who actually gets elected. In situations such as these, the change happens *to* us rather than *because* of us. But other times, we do have opportunities to have some control over change. If there's going to be a big change at home or at school, someone might ask for your involvement and input. Or, if you see that a change needs to be made, you might decide to make that happen. When you do that, you are leading change.

The position of Welsh in the UK is considerably more healthy
than that of Gaelic. It has far more speakers, and fairly consider-
able amounts of time are given to radio and television broadcasts
in Welsh (although not as much as some would like). As in the
case of Gaelic, the effects of the older educational approach
linger on. Many older people today, while being fluent speakers
of Welsh, have never learned to write it. They have to write even
the most intimate of letters in a foreign language, English, and
very often find it difficult to read Standard Welsh. Today the
situation is much improved, and especially since the early 1930s
there has been a change in emphasis. At around that time
Welsh began to be taught seriously in many primary schools in
Welsh-speaking areas, although its role in secondary schools
was very minor. Subsequently, in 1953, a report was published
which received Ministry of Education approval: it suggested that
all children in Wales should be taught both Welsh and English.
This bilingual policy has been widely adopted today, although
the actual situation is rather complex since policy is decided on
an area basis by local education authorities. Generally, however,
one can say that in most parts of Wales, whether anglicized or
not, one can find some schools at both primary and secondary
level where Welsh is taught only as a subject, others where it is
used as a medium along with English, and others where Welsh
is the only medium and English is taught as a subject. Another
interesting development is the institution of nursery schools
which are solely Welsh-speaking but to which many English-
speaking parents are sending their children in order that they
should grow up bilingual. Like, apparently, many Irish people,
some of these Welsh parents feel that by adopting the English
language they or their ancestors have in some way been untrue

However, under the Franco dictatorship Catalan was once
banned completely from schools, and chairs of Catalan language
and literature at the University of Barcelona were abolished.
Catalan text books disappeared, and Catalan children again had
to begin and complete their education in Spanish. Supporters of
Catalan claimed that the Franco government was fundamentally
Castilian nationalist' in character, and clearly it was concerned
about what it regarded as separatist tendencies. Language is a
signal of group identity, and anybody attempting to create a
unified nation-state, particularly of the corporate Franco type,
will find any signalling of a different identity undesirable or
dangerous. Linguistic subjugation (or unification, depending
on one's point of view) is therefore an important strategy in
implementing political subjugation (or unification).
In the later years of the Franco regime the situation of Catalan
was somewhat relaxed. Many books became available and there
were two children's comics and one magazine in the language.
There were still, however, no newspapers, and broadcasting time
was very limited indeed. Most significant of all was that Catalan
remained forbidden in the schools. This meant that upon arrival
in school for the first time, Catalan children were unable to
understand what the teacher was saying - for the first few weeks
at least - and that they grew up unable to read and write in their
own language, unless their parents took the trouble to teach
them these skills at home. The extent of the linguistic problem
involved is partly revealed by the following passage in Catalan
and its Spanish translation.

it has come to become the lingua franca of about 1
million people, with languages native to Papua New Guinea
spoken in many households (Mühlhäusler 1987:178).
It is notable that more parliamentary debates are
conducted in it, and most recently it has been heard
in the law courts.
Tok Pisin vocabulary derives from English,
but also from New Guinea languages, especially Tolai
and, through various other languages, including Ger-
man. In Tok Pisin personal pronouns mi 'I, me, yu
'you' (singular) remain the same whether they serve as
subject or object. In the plural, the distinction is made between
the inclusive form (including the hearer) and the exclusive form
(excluding the hearer), and in all three persons of the plural
the dual (e.g., mitupela 'we two', yutupela 'you two'
is distinct). It is usually indicated, as in yutupela occurs in ad-
dition to the plural for the third person plural occurs in ad-
dition to the possession is indicated by bilong, the predicate
is marked by a particle i, and transitive verbs have the suffix -im.
The language evolves into causative verb forms. Accordingly,
krosim 'to scold' translates as 'I cook my food'. Wanpela lek bilong
em i bruk 'his leg is broken'. Em i krosim mi as 'He scolded me, and
em i kapsaitim petrol 'he spilled the gasoline'.

VizWiz, una nueva aplicación para móviles, proporciona a los discapacitados visuales soluciones
casi en tiempo real a los problemas cotidianos. VizWiz puede, por ejemplo, ayudar a los ciegos a
leer su correo, coordinar sus equipos, entender los menús de los restaurantes, verificar fechas de
vencimiento e interpretar las señales de tráfico. Basta con hacer una foto con el iPhone y enviarla
con la pregunta correspondiente. La aplicación debe su rapidez y precisión a una combinación de
chips informáticos y capacidad intelectual humana al viejo estilo.


Diseñar un programa informático capaz de reconocer texto y distinguir objetos de forma fiable en
el mundo real ha demostrado ser un gran desafío para los investigadores de inteligencia artificial.
Para resolver esto, los investigadores que están tras VizWiz --un equipo formado por científicos
informáticos de varias universidades, entre ellas la Universidad de Rochester-- decidieron
externalizar la tarea de resolución de problemas, dejándola en manos de personas:
concretamente, de los trabajadores en línea de Amazon Mechanical Turk.


Para asegurar que los usuarios obtienen las respuestas lo más rápidamente posible, los
investigadores programaron un sistema de colas inteligente que denominan Quik Turkit para
acelerar las cosas. Quik Turkit recluta trabajadores de Mechanical Turk, incluso mientras un
usuario de VizWiz realiza una foto, de modo que siempre haya alguien dispuesto a responder
una consulta entrante.

Custer, Dawes Act. 15. What led to the start of boomtowns, and what caused their decline? 16. What new invention finally brought an end to the open range on the Great Plains? 17. How did the railroads boost the settlement of the West? 18. Why was wheat a suitable crop to grow on the Great Plains? 19. What events brought the way of life of the Plains Indians to an end? **Critical Thinking** 20. **Analyzing Themes: Economic Factors** Do you think that people moved to and settled in the West primarily for eco- nomic reasons? Why or why not? Why do you think that so many **Drawing Conclusions** people were willing to give up their homes and move to ing towns and homesteads in the West? **Forming an Opinion** How do you think a peaceful settle ment might have been reached between the Native Americans and the U.S. government? **Interpreting Primary Sources** In the late 1860s, the U.S. government adopted a policy of forcing Native Americans onto small reservations in the Black Hills of Dakota and bar ren regions of Oklahoma. The government forced many Native American chiefs to sign treaties and to promise to move onto the reservations. Many Native Americans, how ever, refused to move and fought to maintain their tradi tional way of life. In the excerpt that follows, Satanta, a chief of the Kiowa, responds to the government's policy. Read the excerpt and answer the questions that follow: “I have heard that you intend to settle us on a reser- vation near the mountains. I don't want to settle. I love to roam over the prairies. There I feel free and happy, but when we settle down we grow pale and die. I have laid aside my lance, bow, and shield, and yet I feel safe in your presence. I have told you the truth. I have no little lies hid about me, but I don't know how it is with the commissioners. Are they as clear as I am?  1. تعديل البند (ثانياً/ 1) ليصبح: "تلتزم الشركة بتوفير كافة الخدمات اللوجستية المطلوبة في موعد أقصاه 30 يوماً من تاريخ التوقيع".
 2. إضافة بند جديد (رابعاً/ 5) ينص على: "يحق للطرف الثاني إنهاء العقد في حال تأخر الطرف الأول عن التنفيذ لمدة تتجاوز 15 يوماً دون عذر مقبول".
 3. تعديل الفقرة (خامساً/ 2) المتعلقة بالتعويضات لتشمل بنداً خاصاً بالمسؤولية عن الأضرار غير المباشرة.
 4. إلغاء الفقرة (سادساً/ 3) التي تشير إلى التحكيم كخيار وحيد لتسوية النزاعات، واستبدالها بنص يسمح باللجوء للقضاء المختص.
 5. تعديل قيمة الغرامة التأخيرية في البند (سابعاً/ 1) لتصبح 0.5% من قيمة العقد عن كل يوم تأخير، بحد أقصى 10% من إجمالي القيمة.
 6. إضافة ملحق خاص بتفاصيل المعايير الفنية والجودة المطلوبة للخدمات، ويعد جزءاً لا يتجزأ من العقد.
 7. تعديل آلية الدفع في البند (ثامناً/ 2) لتكون على ثلاث دفعات: 30% دفعة مقدمة، 40% عند الإنجاز المرحلي، و30% عند التسليم النهائي.
 8. إضافة نص صريح يضمن سرية المعلومات المتبادلة بين الطرفين طوال فترة سريان العقد ولمدة سنتين بعد انتهائه.
 9. تعديل فترة الإخطار لإنهاء العقد في البند (تاسعاً/ 1) لتصبح 60 يوماً بدلاً من 30 يوماً.
 10. إدراج شرط يمنع الطرف الأول من التنازل عن التزاماته التعاقدية لأي طرف ثالث دون موافقة خطية مسبقة من الطرف الثاني.
 11. إضافة مادة تتعلق بالقوة القاهرة توضح الإجراءات الواجب اتباعها في حال حدوث ظروف خارجة عن الإرادة تعيق التنفيذ.
 12. تعديل صلاحية العقد لتكون سنة واحدة قابلة للتجديد تلقائياً ما لم يخطر أحد الطرفين الآخر برغبته في عدم التجديد قبل 90 يوماً.
 13. إدراج بند خاص بحقوق الملكية الفكرية يضمن انتقال كافة الحقوق الناتجة عن الخدمات إلى الطرف الثاني فور سداد كامل المستحقات.
 14. تعديل تعريف "الخدمات" في مقدمة العقد ليكون أكثر شمولية وتحديداً لضمان عدم وجود لبس في نطاق العمل.
 15. إضافة شرط يفرض على الطرف الأول تقديم تأمين حسن تنفيذ بنسبة 5% من قيمة العقد الإجمالية.
 16. تعديل اللغة المعتمدة لتفسير العقد لتكون اللغة العربية، وفي حال وجود ترجمة، يعتد بالنص العربي في حال التعارض.
 17. إضافة بند يحدد ساعات العمل الرسمية وقنوات التواصل المعتمدة بين الطرفين لضمان سرعة التنسيق.
 18. مراجعة وتعديل ملاحق العقد الفنية لتتوافق مع التحديثات الأخيرة في المعايير التقنية المعمول بها.
